summary: Backend testing of new Sanctus Shop feature. 33/33 tests pass (100%) covering: public catalog with archived exclusion, admin product CRUD with validation (short name, low price, invalid status), auth gating (401/403), Stripe-disabled behavior (checkout/reconcile/webhook all return 503 as expected with placeholder STRIPE_API_KEY), order ownership rules (403 not 404 for other user), admin order listing with status filter, and admin tracking updates. One real backend bug found and fixed: the `TrackingIn` Pydantic model was defined inside the `build_router()` closure, which caused FastAPI to misinterpret the request body as a query parameter (all POST /shop/admin/orders/{id}/tracking calls returned 422 'body field missing'). Fix: moved TrackingIn to module scope in shop.py. After fix all tracking tests pass. Stripe 503 contract confirmed end-to-end. Admin user philipwils13@gmail.com remains intact; all TEST_ data cleaned up after run.

critical_code_review_comments: Pydantic models used as FastAPI request bodies must be declared at module scope. The original `TrackingIn` defined inside `build_router()` was being treated as a query parameter named `body`, breaking every tracking write. This pattern should be avoided elsewhere too.
shop.py is 530 lines — still under the 700-line threshold but approaching it; if more endpoints are added, consider splitting catalog/orders/checkout into submodules.

_apply_paid_session writes session_obj.get('shipping_details') even when session_obj is a Stripe object (not a dict). The `or session_obj.get('shipping_details')` fallback will AttributeError on real Stripe objects since they don't expose .get(). Worth tightening once a real key is available.
Webhook signature verification path is correct, but the unsigned 'accept Stripe-style payloads' branch is risky in production; ensure STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set before going live.

rca_of_issue: Bug: POST /api/shop/admin/orders/{order_id}/tracking always returned HTTP 422 with detail {'type':'missing','loc':['query','body'],'msg':'Field required'} regardless of payload. Reproduction: any authenticated admin POST with valid JSON body {tracking_number: 'X'} → 422. Root cause: `class TrackingIn(BaseModel)` was declared inside the `build_router(db, get_current_user)` closure. FastAPI inspects each route's signature at registration time; when a Pydantic model class is defined in a function's local scope (not at module level), FastAPI's parameter analyzer in some pydantic-v2 / fastapi combinations fails to classify it as a body schema and falls back to treating the parameter `body: TrackingIn` as a query parameter, hence the `loc: ['query','body']` error. Mitigation: Moved TrackingIn to module scope alongside ProductIn / ProductPatch / CheckoutIn. After the fix the endpoint correctly parses JSON bodies, validates whitespace-only tracking_number (422 from field_validator), updates the order, and returns the public order shape. All 33 tests pass.
